title: Product of Segments of Chords OQ-01: 3D and General Generalization
description: Formal proof that the intersecting chords theorem (power of a point) extends to spheres in ℝ³ and to any real inner product space: the product of chord segment lengths through an interior point equals r² − d², invariant across all secant lines.

meta.author: Lean Genius
originalContributions: Dimension-independent proof of the chord quadratic equation in any real inner product space
Power of a point theorem for spheres in arbitrary inner product spaces (not just 2D)
Explicit 3D corollary with Sphere3D structure and EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)
Vieta product formula applied to derive |t₁|·|t₂| = r² − ‖P−O‖²

overview.historicalContext: The intersecting chords theorem (Wiedijk #55) states that for two chords AB and CD intersecting at P inside a circle, PA·PB = PC·PD. This is the 2D power of a point theorem. The natural generalization asks whether the same invariance holds for spheres in ℝ³ or higher-dimensional spheres.
overview.problemStatement: Prove that for a sphere with center O and radius r in any real inner product space, if P is an interior point (‖P−O‖ < r), then for any unit direction dir, the two intersection parameters t₁, t₂ of the line P+t·dir with the sphere satisfy |t₁|·|t₂| = r² − ‖P−O‖². In particular, this product is independent of dir.
overview.proofStrategy: The chord intersection equation ‖(P−O) + t·dir‖ = r expands via the inner product to t² + 2t⟨P−O,dir⟩ + (‖P−O‖² − r²) = 0. This is a monic quadratic in t, so Vieta's formulas give t₁·t₂ = ‖P−O‖² − r². Since P is interior, t₁ and t₂ have opposite signs, so |t₁|·|t₂| = r² − ‖P−O‖². The proof uses only inner product axioms, making it dimension-independent.
keyInsights: The chord equation depends only on inner products and norms, which are available in any inner product space
Vieta's product formula for the monic quadratic directly gives t₁·t₂
Interior point condition (‖P−O‖ < r) ensures t₁·t₂ < 0, giving |t₁·t₂| = −(t₁·t₂) = r² − ‖P−O‖²
The 3D explicit corollary reduces to the general theorem via coordinate translation
prerequisites: NormedAddCommGroup and inner product lemmas (inner_add_left, inner_smul_right, etc.)

conclusion.summary: This file proves 6 theorems (plus 1 private lemma) with 0 sorries and 0 axioms, establishing the power of a point theorem in full generality for any real inner product space, with an explicit 3D corollary.
conclusion.implications: The theorem confirms that the power of a point is a purely inner-product-space phenomenon, valid in any dimension. The proof technique (chord quadratic + Vieta) applies uniformly from ℝ² to infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
openQuestions: Generalize to complex inner product spaces or Hilbert spaces over other fields
Prove the analogous result for the external case (P outside the sphere): PA·PB = d² − r²
